transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Yeah, um… I guess what brings me in is people have started noticing how I move, which sounds weird. Like sometimes I’m really slow, like I’m underwater or something—taking forever to answer a question or even get out of a chair.

And then other times I’m just pacing around my apartment, rubbing my hands like I’m trying to shake off a bad customer service call. I do get a lot of those calls, actually—people yelling about stuff I can’t even fix—but, yeah, the main thing is it’s noticeable now.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

Yeah… I mean, most of the time since this all started, it’s kind of been there. Like not always dramatic, you know, not every single day is me staring at a wall or anything, but… sadness is there in the background.

And guilt too, like I’ll feel bad about stuff that probably isn’t even that big. I’ll lose interest in things, and sleep’s been messed up. Some weeks it’s lighter, like I can get through work and seem normal enough, but it doesn’t really go away.
Have you been hearing or seeing things that other people don’t seem to?

Yeah… mostly hearing things, I guess. Not like a whole conversation, but I’ll hear the old headset beep from work, like when a call’s coming in, even when my laptop is closed and there’s no phone ringing.

And sometimes it’s like a supervisor kind of voice saying my name, or saying “too slow.” Which is… I mean, I get told to speed up at work all the time, not exactly like that maybe, but customer service is all timers and metrics and—sorry. Yeah. Other people don’t seem to hear it.
Have you ever heard those voices at a time when you were not feeling depressed?

Yeah… I think so. Like, there have been stretches for a few weeks where I wasn’t really feeling depressed in the same way—more like I could get up, do laundry, answer emails, make dinner, that kind of normal.

But I’d still hear that supervisor-type voice sometimes, or I’d be sitting there and feel sure the old ticketing software was flagging me for something. Which is dumb because we don’t even use that system the same way anymore, but I’d still get that feeling.
Have you ever had a period where you felt unusually energized or high, needing much less sleep than usual?

Um… I don’t think so? Not really “high,” I guess. I mean, sometimes I’ll get a weird burst where I clean the kitchen at like 11 p.m., but that’s usually because I put it off all week and then I’m annoyed looking at it.

Less sleep… my sleep gets messed up, but I wouldn’t say I’m energized from it. It’s more like I’m tired and still awake, if that makes sense. Like scrolling through random stuff or worrying about work schedules, and then suddenly I’m reading about air fryers or old game shows or something and it’s 2 a.m.

So… no, I don’t think I’ve had a period where I felt unusually energized like that.
When you get very slowed down, do you ever stay in one position for a long time even when someone is trying to get you to move?

Not exactly like someone trying to move me and I just won’t, I don’t think. But… when I get really overwhelmed, I do kind of freeze.

Like I’ll be in the kitchen and realize I’ve been standing there with my coffee mug halfway up to my mouth, just… stuck. Or I’ll walk the same little loop near the couch for no real reason, like I meant to do something but can’t land on what it was. It’s embarrassing, because then I’m like, okay, why am I pacing between the lamp and the TV stand like it’s a job.
Did these movement problems begin after any medical illness, seizure, head injury, or drug use?

I don’t think so… I mean, not that I can connect it to.

Like, I didn’t have some big thing where I got hurt and then suddenly I was freezing in the kitchen or whatever. It’s more like it just sort of happens when I’m overwhelmed, but I can’t point to a medical thing. I don’t really know what would count, honestly. I mean, I’ve bumped my head like anyone has, but not like… a whole event. And drug use, no, not something like that.

Sorry, I’m kind of circling it—basically, I don’t think it started after any of those things.
Was there ever a period of at least 2 weeks when you were hearing the voice even though you were not depressed?

Yeah… I think so. There have been times, like a few weeks maybe, where I wasn’t really in that low place. I was getting up, doing errands, handling work stuff—well, mostly handling it, because the ticketing system at work is a whole separate nightmare and it always freezes at the worst time—

But, yeah, during stretches where my mood felt closer to normal, I’d still hear that supervisor voice. Or I’d feel really sure the old ticketing software was flagging me somehow, like it was marking me out. So it wasn’t only when I was depressed, if that’s what you mean.
Have you become much less emotionally expressive, like your face or voice feels flat to other people?

Yeah… people have said that. My friends especially. They’ll be telling me something important and I guess my face doesn’t really… do much. Or my voice comes out kind of flat, even if I do care.

It’s not that I don’t want to talk to them. I just end up giving these short answers, like “yeah” or “that sucks,” and then I avoid making plans because it feels like too much to keep up with. Then they think I’m mad or bored, and I’m not, I’m just… hard to read now, I guess.
At any point, did the voices or feeling of being flagged at work continue when you were not feeling depressed at all?

Yeah, that did happen. I mean, not constantly, but there were stretches—maybe a few weeks—where I wasn’t really depressed. I was getting up, doing errands, getting through work stuff, and I felt more normal, or close to it.

But the supervisor voice would still show up, or I’d still get this strong feeling that the old ticketing software was flagging me somehow. Which sounds weird when I say it out loud, but at the time it felt really real. So… yeah, it wasn’t only when I was feeling low.
Looking back over the whole time this has been going on, has depression been present for most of it?

Yeah… I think so. Looking back, most of the time since this all started, there’s been some level of it there. Like sadness, guilt, not really being interested in stuff, sleep being off.

Some weeks it’s lighter, like I can still get through things and I’ll think, “Okay, maybe I’m fine,” but then it’s still kind of sitting in the background. It’s like when my apartment has that low hum from the fridge—sorry, random—but you stop noticing it until it gets quiet for a second. That’s kind of how it feels. The depression hasn’t always been intense, but it’s been there most of the time.
